chunks: Zur'ah narrated from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who purchases a slave while he has run away from his owner, he said:

It is not valid for him unless he purchases something else along with him and says, 'I purchase from you this item and your slave for such and such amount.' If he is unable to obtain the slave, then the price he paid will be for what he purchased from him.

key_terms.آبِقٌ: a slave who has run away from his owner
key_terms.الثَّمَنُ: the price or payment in the transaction
key_terms.شَيْئًا آخَرَ: another item included with the main sale
key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not valid or not proper in this legal context
key_terms.نَقَدَهُ: he paid it over in cash or tendered it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying an absconded slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about purchasing an absconded slave. The Imam عليه السلام states that such a transaction is only valid when another item is included in the sale, so that if the slave cannot be recovered, the payment remains allocated to the other purchased item.
